title: Give SignInActions' TapGestureRecognizer a disposal owner instead of rebuilding it every build()
why: SignInActions is a StatelessWidget, so every build() (e.g. each time isLoading flips) allocates a brand-new TapGestureRecognizer that nothing ever calls .dispose() on. The framework does not manage recognizer lifecycle automatically; Flutter's own guidance is to create such recognizers once in a State and dispose them in State.dispose(). The same pattern also exists in signup_screen.dart:825, so it's a small but repeated hygiene gap, not a one-off typo.
recommendation: Hoist the 'Register' tap handling into a small stateful owner (or the already-stateful parent SignInScreen) that creates the TapGestureRecognizer once and disposes it in dispose().
acceptance_criteria: the TapGestureRecognizer used for the Register span is created once and disposed via a State.dispose() rather than reallocated on every SignInActions.build()
